sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Cherry Hill?
sections.html:
The Cherry Hill Township Tax Collector bills and collects property tax, and the same office handles township sewer charges. It is in Room 108 of the municipal building at 820 Mercer Street, and the phone is 856-488-7880. The office also acts as the collecting agent for the public school district, the fire district and Camden County, so one bill covers all of them.

Value is a separate matter. The township assessor sets assessments, and appeals go to the Camden County Board of Taxation in Blackwood, not to the collector. If you plan to sell, keep those two questions apart. The township's main number is 856-665-6500, and the assessor and collector both work from 820 Mercer Street: the collector tells you what you owe, the assessor and county board tell you whether the value behind it can be challenged.

sections.h2: What is Cherry Hill like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Cherry Hill covers 24.07 square miles of land in northern Camden County, bounded by Pennsauken Creek on the east and the Cooper River on the south. It began as Delaware Township in 1844, took the Cherry Hill name in 1961, and grew in the postwar suburban boom around the Cherry Hill Mall, which opened in October 1961 as the first enclosed mall in the eastern United States. Before that, Quaker settlers founded a hamlet called Colestown in the late 1600s, and 19th century farms in the township supplied produce to the Campbell's plant in Camden. TD Bank has its headquarters in the township, and Melitta USA roasts coffee here.

Neighborhood names buyers search by include Erlton, Barclay, Kingston, Greentree, Springdale, Old Orchard, Woodcrest and Ellisburg. Interstate 295 has three exits in the township, and Routes 38, 41, 70 and 154 cross it. The PATCO station at Woodcrest and NJ Transit's Atlantic City Line stop give commuters a route into Philadelphia. The school district runs 19 schools, including 12 elementary schools, three middle schools and two traditional high schools.

  • Census Bureau estimate for July 2025: 79,965 people, up from 74,565 at the 2020 base.
  • Median owner-occupied home value, 2020 through 2024: $386,300.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 76.5 percent.
  • Median household income: $121,502, and 20.7 percent of residents are 65 or older.

sections.h2: When are Cherry Hill property taxes due?
sections.html:
Cherry Hill taxes are due on August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1, with a 10-day grace period that moves to the next business day if the tenth falls on a weekend or holiday. The office mails bills twice a year: in July for the third and fourth quarters and in January for the first and second. Not receiving a bill does not excuse the payment or the interest.

Payments must arrive by the end of the grace period, because New Jersey does not allow the collector to accept postmarks. After that, interest runs back to the original due date at 8 percent a year on the first $1,500 and 18 percent on anything above it. Unpaid balances can enter the tax sale process, which must finish by June 30, and during that process only cash or a cashier's check is accepted.

The township's share pays for police, 49 parks, planning and zoning, road repair, snow removal, leaf collection, trash and recycling hauling and the library. The township maintains 246.81 of its 309.36 miles of road, with Camden County, the state and the Turnpike Authority responsible for the rest. The township's page puts the average home at $227,000 assessed and the average annual bill at $11,279.63.

sections.h2: How can you pay a Cherry Hill tax or sewer bill?
sections.html:
There are five ways to pay, and the right one depends on how close you are to the deadline. Allow five business days if you use your bank's bill-pay service, because the bank may mail a check.

  • Drop off cash or a check at Room 108, or use the mail slot on the double doors at the entrance if the building is closed.
  • Mail a check to the Tax Collector's Office, 820 Mercer Street, Cherry Hill, NJ 08002.
  • Pay online with a card or e-check. The payment processor adds a 2.39 percent fee for cards and 99 cents for e-check, and the township charges nothing.
  • Use your bank's bill-pay with "Township of Cherry Hill" as payee and your numeric account number only.
  • Pay by phone: 855-472-2993 for taxes and 855-472-2990 for sewer.

Card and debit payments cannot be taken at the counter or by phone with the office staff. The office also sends email reminders about a week before each due date to residents who sign up.

sections.h2: What does Cherry Hill charge for sewer, and who gets a discount?
sections.html: Residential sewer is billed once a year as a flat fee due April 1, and commercial sewer is billed twice a year, on November 1 and May 1, based on water use. Homeowners aged 60 or older who live in the house can take a 10 percent discount by showing proof of age to the Tax Collector. Sewer is billed apart from tax, so the closing agent should ask the collector whether it is paid to date.

sections.h2: Can you appeal a Cherry Hill assessment?
sections.html:
Yes, through the Camden County Board of Taxation, by April 1 or by May 1 where the township has just revalued. The petition must be received by 4:00 p.m., and you must keep paying through the first quarter while the case runs. Evidence is up to five comparable sales, not the assessments of neighbors. The township's own breakdown puts the average assessment at $227,000, a useful yardstick when you compare your notice to the street around you.

Appeal only the value, never the amount of tax. Your argument is what the house was worth on October 1 of the year before the tax year, set against the town's average ratio. If the county board lowers the value, that judgment holds for the year and the two that follow unless a revaluation or an added assessment changes it. A further appeal goes to the Tax Court of New Jersey within 45 days.

sections.h2: What if you owe tax when you sell in Cherry Hill?
sections.html:
You can sell with tax owing, as long as the balance is paid at closing from the sale money. Ask the collector for a payoff dated for the closing and keep the last bill handy for the title company. Give the current bill to the buyer or the title company so the next installment is paid correctly.

  • Check whether the current quarter falls inside the grace period before you close.
  • Confirm the sewer account is paid to date.
  • If a lien has been sold at the tax sale, the lien holder, not the township, is owed the redemption amount.

faqs.q: What is the grace period for Cherry Hill property tax?
faqs.a: Ten days after each due date, extended to the next business day if the tenth is a weekend or holiday. The payment must be received in the office by then, because postmarks are not accepted.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Cherry Hill taxes?
faqs.a: Pay at the Tax Collector's Office, 820 Mercer Street, Room 108, by mail, online, by phone or through bank bill-pay. Call 856-488-7880 for help.

faqs.q: Does Cherry Hill offer a sewer discount for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. Homeowners aged 60 and older who live in the property get 10 percent off residential sewer with proof of age.

faqs.q: How much interest does Cherry Hill charge on late tax?
faqs.a: Eight percent a year on the first $1,500 of the delinquency and 18 percent on the amount above it, counted from the original due date.

faqs.q: Who hears a Cherry Hill assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The Camden County Board of Taxation, which sits at 509 Lakeland Road in Blackwood. The deadline is April 1, or May 1 after a township revaluation.
